card.title: Free HTTPS, no DNS setup
card.description: Serve this dashboard at {{domain}} over HTTPS with a real Let's Encrypt certificate. The hostname resolves to this server on its own, so there is nothing to configure at a registrar.
card.noPublicIp: This server's public IP address is not known, so a zero-DNS hostname cannot be built. Set APP_PUBLIC_HOST to the IP on the control plane and restart it, or use your own domain below.
card.emailHelp: Any inbox you read works. Certificates are free and renew on their own: Let's Encrypt only emails you if one is about to expire and could not renew.
card.stagingLabel: Test with Let's Encrypt staging first
card.stagingHelp: Staging certificates are not trusted by browsers, but it has no meaningful rate limits. Use it to prove ports 80 and 443 are reachable.
card.pending: Requesting a certificate for {{domain}}. This usually takes under a minute.
card.issuedDetail: Issued by {{issuer}}, expires {{date}}. Renewal is automatic.
card.stagingIssued: This is a staging certificate, so browsers will show a warning. Turn staging off and run it again to get a trusted one.
card.dashboardUrlFailed: Could not save the dashboard URL.
card.preflightBody: This server could not reach itself on port {{ports}} at its public address. Let's Encrypt must reach port 80 (and 443 for renewals) from the internet. Open them in your cloud firewall or run the firewall step in setup. This check can be wrong behind some routers, so wait for the certificate before changing anything.

hint.unreachable: Let's Encrypt could not reach this server on port 80. Open ports 80 and 443 in your firewall and your cloud provider's security group, then try again.
hint.rate_limited: Let's Encrypt is rate limiting this hostname. Wait before retrying, and use staging while you debug.
hint.dns: The hostname did not resolve to this server. Check that the detected public IP is correct.
hint.caa: A CAA DNS record forbids Let's Encrypt from issuing for this hostname.
hint.unknown: Let's Encrypt refused the request. The full response is below and in the control plane log.

fallback.title: Automatic app hostnames
fallback.description: Apps without a domain get https://<app>.<dashed-ip>.sslip.io with automatic TLS, so a fresh deploy is reachable with zero DNS.
fallback.toggleLabel: Give apps without a domain an automatic hostname
fallback.noPublicHost: No public address detected. Set APP_PUBLIC_HOST on the control plane to turn this on.

network.off: Automatic hostnames are turned off for this server.
network.noPublicHost: No public IP is known for this server, so no automatic hostname can be built. Set APP_PUBLIC_HOST on the control plane.

wizard.sslipReady: HTTPS is ready on the free hostname. You can continue, or set up your own domain too.

certTable.internalHint: Signed by this server's own short-lived CA and renewed automatically. Browsers show a warning until you enable HTTPS.
